candidates.buyer: About 280 small accommodation properties plus dive and game-fishing operators, many family-run and village-based
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.evidence: https://solomons.gov.sb/?p=901 ; https://solomons.gov.sb/?p=900 ; https://www.solomontimes.com/news/hotels-to-achieve-minimum-standards-accreditation/9178 . Sources are about 2019 and the programme may have changed. Tourism Act text and any levy or guest-register rule not found.
candidates.name: C30. Tourism accommodation and operator licence and Minimum Standards compliance kit (guest houses, lodges, homestays, dive and game-fishing operators)
candidates.trigger: Tourism Solomons licence renewed annually, and required before an HCC business licence; Minimum Standards and Classification programme (8 categories incl. homestay and ecolodge) with periodic assessment; stacks with HCC or provincial licence, TIN and SINPF
candidates.unchecked: Current fees and renewal dates, legal basis, and whether the classification re-assessment is recurring. Competitor search in the local language not run (search budget used up). Willingness to pay of village lodges is likely low.

candidates.buyer: Owners of commercial boats carrying passengers, cargo or fish: provincial water taxis, dive boats, fishing boats. Provincial governments hold the lists, which would make them a second possible buyer.
candidates.category: 32. Small craft and vessel licensing under SIMA
candidates.existing: None seen; SIMA and provinces keep lists on paper or in Word (not confirmed)
candidates.name: C32. Small craft (under 10 m) annual licence, inspection and register workflow for commercial boat owners
candidates.trigger: SIMA Guidelines for Small Craft Safety Operations (circular March 2026): licence number on both sides of hull, certificate carried on board, annual inspection within 1 month either side of the licence anniversary, fees paid to the issuing province, provincial Small Craft List kept by SIMA and provinces. New class system (Class A etc.).
candidates.unchecked: Fee levels, how many boats are licensed in practice, enforcement, whether guidelines are binding or still advisory. Competitor search not run. Most owners are poor and the main buyer may be the state (out of scope).

candidates.buyer: Licensed exporters and cocoa wet-bean and dry-bean buyers, copra traders (number not found, probably dozens)
candidates.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders
candidates.name: C33. CEMA export licence and buying-licence compliance for cocoa, copra and palm oil traders
candidates.trigger: Only CEMA or its licensees may export copra, cocoa, coconut products, palm oil, coffee and spices. Licence valid 12 months (WTO profile: SBD 5,000 cocoa/copra, SBD 50,000 palm oil). Cocoa Trading Licence structure in the 2013 regulations; coconut regulations 2016; CEMA wants statistics and financial reports from licence holders (an expectation, not a confirmed rule).
candidates.unchecked: Whether purchase and stock returns are actually mandatory, and their form. Competitor search not run. Small buyer pool and cocoa dispute news suggest a politically messy sector.

candidates.buyer: Licensed beche-de-mer exporters and buyers (small number, seasonal)
candidates.existing: None seen; K03 (tuna catch documentation, Noro e-port, TRACES) covers a different species and buyers
candidates.name: C34. Beche-de-mer (sea cucumber) season reporting pack: monthly log, buying summary, holding report, export declaration and CBSI Specific Authority to Export
candidates.trigger: Sea Cucumber Management Plan schedules (2014 amendment): conditions for export licence, sea cucumber monthly log, export declaration form, end-of-season holding report, monthly buying summary. CBSI Exchange Control Notice 04/2021 requires a Specific Authority to Export with a market price certificate before shipping. News alleges undervaluation of exports, so authorities have a reason to enforce.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the fishery is open (seasons, bans), current forms, number of licensed exporters. Competitor search not run.

candidates.buyer: Foreign-owned shops, restaurants and contractors (many small, e.g. Asian-owned) and local companies without an accountant
candidates.category: 35. Foreign investment, business names and work permits; also 15, 26, 28
candidates.existing: Company Haus / solomonbusinessregistry.gov.sb online registry (state portal) handles filings; local accountants
candidates.name: C35. Foreign-owned small business annual compliance bundle: Foreign Investment annual survey, Company Haus annual return, business-name renewal and work permits
candidates.trigger: Foreign Investment Act 2005 s7: annual survey within 2 months of financial year-end on the prescribed form; Foreign Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (Gazette 31 Oct 2025, regs 15 and 16 replaced, content unseen); company annual return in the chosen month; Business Names (Amendment) Regulations 2024 reset fees; work permits for every non-citizen worker with a local-availability test, applied for to the Commissioner of Labour.
candidates.unchecked: Contents of the 2025 amendment, whether the annual survey is enforced, penalties, size of the foreign-investor population. Competitor search not run. A done-for-you service rather than software is more likely.

candidates.buyer: Small employers with a few staff, including households that employ workers (any employer paid SBD 20 or more for 6 or more days a month)
candidates.existing: SINPF's own EDI template; sinpfportal.com is member-facing only (not confirmed as filing portal)
candidates.name: C36. SINPF monthly contribution schedule (EDI Excel template) preparation for small employers
candidates.trigger: NPF Act (Cap 109): register within 14 days; monthly contribution schedule must be filed in the Excel-based EDI template since July 2015; payment at SINPF offices or by bank
candidates.trigger_note: Same buyer and payroll-style duty as K05 (rejected); recorded for completeness.
candidates.unchecked: Penalties and late-payment interest not found. Likely falls under generic payroll (out of scope).

candidates.buyer: Landowner sawmill operators and small millers
candidates.name: C37. Timber levy, mill licence and felling-licence returns for small portable-sawmill and Type B landowner millers
candidates.trigger: Timber (Levy and Mill Licensing) Regulations: mill licence application or renewal to the Commissioner of Forest Resources, timber levy on timber sold in Solomon Islands or exported; Type B licences above 1,000 cubic metres per year or with extraction machinery need plans approved; annual harvest and coupe plans required. A 2017 exemption order for teak woodlots required records of logs within 14 days of export or sale.
candidates.unchecked: Whether small portable mills file any returns; the ministry reportedly has poor record management. Buyers are mostly informal and cash-poor.

candidates.buyer: Gold dealers, alluvial miners, sand and gravel suppliers
candidates.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors; also 4
candidates.name: C38. Gold dealer, alluvial miner and building-materials permit compliance
candidates.trigger: Mines and Minerals Act (Cap 42): Alluvial Miner's Permit (citizens only), Gold Dealer's Licence, Building Materials Permit (10 years, up to 0.5 sq km, landowner consent)
candidates.unchecked: No recurring report format found; permits are long-lived, so low frequency.

candidates.buyer: CBSI-licensed money changers (min. capital SBD 50,000, fee SBD 2,000) and money transfer services (SBD 200,000, fee SBD 5,000), all renewed annually
candidates.name: C39. FX dealer and money changer licence and reporting pack (restricted dealers and money changers)
candidates.trigger: Exchange Control Act 1976 s3 and Regulation s20; Public Notice 03.2024 on mandatory licensing; restricted dealers capped at SBD 10,000 per customer per month outbound; cash dealers under MLPCA 2010
candidates.unchecked: Only a handful of licensees; specific periodic return forms not found.

candidates.buyer: Bars, clubs, restaurants, bottle shops and hotels with liquor licences
candidates.evidence: https://www.sibconline.com.sb/?p=29735 ; https://pacliirms.paclii.org/sb/other/SBGovGaz/1998/27.pdf (evidence is 1990s Gazette notices plus an undated SIBC article, so current practice is unverified)
candidates.name: C40. Liquor licence renewal and objection tracking (Honiara Liquor Licensing Board)
candidates.trigger: Liquor Act (Cap 33): renewals advertised in the Gazette with a hearing at the Central Magistrates Court; objections in writing to the Board chairman (s23)
candidates.unchecked: Current Act and process, number of licences, Board functioning (chair vacancy reported about 2019).

candidates.buyer: Small shops, transport owners and traders in Honiara and Guadalcanal who must hold an HCC or provincial licence
candidates.existing: None seen; it would overlap K02 (HCC transport) and K06 (market fees, rejected)

candidates.trigger: HCC (Regulation of Business Licences) Ordinance 2011, fees reset every year by the Fees, Rates and Charges Ordinance (2025 version seen); counter-only payment on Mendana Avenue; SICCI objected to fee increases in 2023; Guadalcanal Business and Hawkers Licensing (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 and Rennell and Bellona schedule changes in March 2025; HCC inspection drives
candidates.unchecked: Whether HCC has an online payment option (none found), what fraction of SMEs are non-compliant, willingness to pay. Competitor search not run. Generic-calendar risk.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No household-employer regime found. The PacLII Labour Act text defines 'undertaking' to exclude domestic establishments, so general employment duties likely do not reach households. No source on SINPF registration of household employers (unverified). Nothing new beyond the SINPF employer duty seen in the first pass.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No scrap-metal dealer licence or register found. Only an exchange-control layer: CBSI notice that minerals are exported under Specific Authority to Export (cbsi.com.sb/?p=13519) and a Nov 2022 gazette adding minerals to the General Authority. Scrap metal not mentioned. Tiny trade.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Solomon Islands pawnbroker or second-hand dealer statute found; results were NZ, Victoria and Malawi only. Only an HCC business licence (2011 Ordinance, free per tradeportal) applies.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or dealer licensing found. Used-vehicle import is open (no age limit, no mandatory inspection per exporter blogs, unverified); the only duty is vehicle registration and an HCC business licence. Police run roadside checks. Nothing to build on.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Diseases of Animals Act (animal movement and quarantine, last updated 1996) and Diseases of Animals (Control of Movement of Cattle) Rules 1964 (written permit; status unclear). Biosecurity Act 2013 has ministerial import bans (2020 live pig ban). No inter-island livestock register or recurring report found. Market vendors already K06.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No abattoir or slaughter licence or meat-inspection regime found. Butchery appears only as an HCC business licence category (2007 gazette fee schedule, issuing authority unconfirmed). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeping or honey rule found in one combined search; nothing registered. Negligible sector.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No Veterinary Act or vet registration found. Only the Diseases of Animals Act (competent authority, quarantine). Very few private vets. Nothing to build on.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: MMERE site: permits from the Water Resources Management Division and SIWA are needed to divert surface water or extract groundwater (River Waters Act 1996 and SIWA Act 1992). No separate driller licence found. The 2023 Water Resources Act in my query was not confirmed. Few operators; permit processing is manual (unverified).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Environment Act 1998 s.38 requires a licence for prescribed premises discharging waste. Whether septic or desludging operators are covered was not confirmed. SPREP says waste regulation is fragmented. HCC plus three private contractors collect commercial waste to Ranadi dump (older JICA/SPREP report). No recurring reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Safety at Work Act 1982 s.17 and Sch 2 with 1998 gazette fee notice (pacliirms.austlii.edu.au/sb/other/SBGovGaz/1998/46.pdf): registration and inspection certificates for boilers, pressure systems and lifting machines, fines of $1,000. Labour Division OSH Unit inspects. Current fees and any amendment unverified; no reform bill found. See candidate.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Rural supplies run by community water committees (Environmental Health Division support, 2024 PaCWaM+ report). Western Province Rural Water Supply Ordinance 1995 (status unverified). No recurring reporting duty or licence for private vendors or bottled water found. Donor and NGO territory; no buyer who pays.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Safety at Work (Pesticides) Regulations 1983: anyone importing, selling, supplying or using a pesticide must apply to the Registrar (MAL Pesticides Registration Unit, solomons.gov.sb/?p=38975, undated notice). Product registration, not dealer licensing. Very few importers; weak.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Honiara City Council sets grave fees by annual Fees, Rates and Charges ordinance (2023: $400 adult, $150 child grave). No funeral-home licensing found. Council-run, so the buyer would be the state. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Petroleum Act Cap 81 (storage permits, fees by tank capacity per 1998 notice). Prices are gazetted monthly under the Price Control Act Cap 64 (PAC; suppliers Markwarth Oil and South Pacific Oil; LPG Geogas and Gafung). Regulated retail margin 75 cents per litre; a Dec 2025 review found retailers getting extra supplier rebates above the regulated allowance. Few retailers, duopoly suppliers. See candidate.

result.reason: Duty is real: the Solomon Islands Visitors Bureau Act 1996 (reprint current Feb 2024) Part III bans unlicensed tourist enterprises. The 1999 Regulations set a Form 1 application and a $100 fee (possibly outdated) and a monthly bed levy return. The government site says licences are renewed annually and are a prerequisite to the Honiara City Council licence. Minimum Standards assessment applies (8 categories; 98 of 280 properties assessed by 2019). I found no software or state portal doing the job, but searched only in English. Current fees were not found and the classification renewal cycle is unconfirmed. Market is small (about 160 to 280 properties), the payers are low-income village lodges, and the paperwork is one annual form plus a monthly levy return. Low willingness to pay.

The duty is partly confirmed, but the SIMA guidelines are an interim national framework. The search summary says SIMA intends a future maritime order under Part IX of its Act, so licensing is not yet firmly binding. I could not read the PDF (binary), so fees, penalties and the inspection rule are unchecked. The March 2026 circular says craft under 10 m must be licensed annually by SIMA and provinces, with inspections and the licence number on the hull. No competing software or portal turned up, but only one search ran. The market is unknown (SIMA says small craft capacity is unknown). The likely buyer is the state or provinces (out of scope), and owners are poor with low willingness to pay. Weak case.

Duty to hold a CEMA licence is real: only CEMA or licensees may export copra, cocoa, palm oil and others. The 2005 and 2013 gazettes set cocoa conditions, and the WTO profile gives SBD 5,000 (cocoa and copra) and SBD 50,000 (palm oil), valid 12 months. I found no confirmed mandatory recurring return or filing duty. Only a CEMA official said sharing statistics and financial reports is important. CEMA has also launched a state data management system built with PHAMA Plus and Insight Pacific, so a state tool may cover reporting. The buyer pool is small, probably dozens, and a once-a-year licence renewal is a thin workflow. Deregulation was floated. The Act text and the current licence-return rules were not read.
